card.name: Linking words before inhaled asthma drugs
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as of, to, compared, comparing and an opening parenthesis, placed just before a named inhaled asthma drug (ICS, LABA, budesonide/formoterol, salmeterol, fluticasone). Seen in asthma label text.

modes.label: Comparison wording
modes.description: Words like compared, comparing or to that introduce a comparison between inhaled steroid and long-acting beta agonist treatments.
modes.example: one trial<< compared>> budesonide and formoterol

modes.label: Of or use of before a drug
modes.description: The word of after dose, safety or use, right before an inhaled drug brand or generic name.
modes.example: increasing the dose<< of>> Fluticasone Propionate/Salm

modes.label: Joining ICS and LABA
modes.description: A parenthesis or and linking an inhaled steroid with a long-acting beta agonist.

card.writes: It pushes toward inhaled-steroid and long-acting beta agonist terms such as ICS, LAB and rescue.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words just before the name of an inhaled asthma medicine is expected.
